rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass across the four views, with a recognizable dominant body and a small carved/notched condition that gives some address to the access edge. It is not coherently resolved as only one-view imagery, and the solids do not visibly collide across views, so it passes the massing sanity checks. The downside is that the public void is modest and more like a shallow entry subtraction than a fully legible courtyard or court, so the neighborhood-living brief is only partially expressed. The silhouette is acceptable but somewhat box-led, with the notch doing most of the spatial work; this keeps repair integrity high but limits section/program expressiveness. Overall it is program-plausible for a compact neighborhood living / mixed-use object, but it would benefit from a stronger carved void or clearer access-side gesture.
